title: The class pet debate
text:
Ms Lestari's Year 5 class are choosing a class pet. Wulan and Kofi are speaking at the front of the room.

Ms Lestari: Wulan, you wanted a rabbit. Tell us why.

Wulan: A rabbit is soft and gentle, and everybody can stroke it. It would be the perfect friend for our class. Everyone would love it, and nobody could possibly be unhappy with a rabbit.

Kofi: I disagree. A rabbit needs a big hutch and fresh grass every day, and it needs to run outside. Our classroom is small. I think we should have fish.

Wulan: Fish are boring! You cannot even cuddle a fish.

Kofi: You can watch them, though. My cousin keeps a tank at home, and it is the calmest corner of his whole house. Fish also stay quiet, so they would not disturb anyone who is reading.

Ms Lestari: Wulan, can you answer Kofi's point about the space?

Wulan: Well, the rabbit could live in the garden during the day. But I suppose someone would have to feed it at weekends and in the holidays.

Kofi: That is my worry. Fish can be left with an automatic feeder for a weekend. But a rabbit cannot be left alone for three days.

Ms Lestari: That is a fair point. Is there anything about fish that worries you, Wulan?

Wulan: Only that they might die if the water gets dirty. I would feel awful.

Kofi: We could take turns to clean the tank, and Ms Lestari could teach us how. I have already written a plan.

Ms Lestari: A plan is a good start. Shall we vote after the break? Whichever pet wins, we must promise to look after it properly.

Wulan: All right. I still think rabbits are better, but I will vote for whichever one has the best plan for the holidays.

Kofi: That is a sensible way to choose.
